criteria.criterion: After a run, new listings have description, images, shipping cost and seller filled from their item pages.
criteria.plannedImplementation: ScrapeRunService.Run calls IItemDetailFetchService.FetchDetails(jobId, ct) after the search upsert completes. ItemDetailFetchService.FetchDetails loads targets via IItemDetailStore.GetListingsNeedingDetail (listings in the job with DetailFetchedUtc null), fetches each item page through IScrapeClient, parses it with the marketplace-matching IItemPageParser, and calls ItemDetailStore.ApplyItemDetail, which copies Description, DescriptionStatus="ok", Seller, ShippingCost, OriginalPrice, Likes, PostedUtc and ImageUrls (serialised via ListingImageUrlsJson) onto the ListingEntity and sets DetailFetchedUtc.
criteria.plannedVerification: NewListingsGetItemDetailFetchedAfterARunTests.Should_populate_description_images_shipping_cost_and_seller_from_the_item_page_after_a_run runs ScrapeRunService end to end against a real SQLite database with a stub IScrapeClient returning a captured Mercari active item-page fixture, then asserts the persisted listing's Description, ImageUrls, ShippingCost and Seller match the fixture's content. Observable outcome: a completed run leaves a caller able to read full item detail for a listing it just discovered.

criteria.criterion: A sold listing from a sold search ends the run with SoldDate and SoldPrice set and a history row recorded, with exactly one Sold history row per sale (review fix: the original unconditional-add design double-counted every sale against #43's ListingUpserter, which already writes an InitialScrape-or-StatusUpdate Sold row when a listing is first observed sold).
criteria.plannedImplementation: ItemDetailStore.ApplyItemDetail now captures wasSold = listing.IsSold before mutating the entity, then passes it into ApplySoldDetail. When detail.Status == "Sold": the listing-level SoldPrice/SoldDate/ItemStatus/IsSold are updated exactly as before; for history, if wasSold is true, ApplySoldDetail loads the most recent existing ListingStatusChangeEntity with Status == "Sold" for that listing and enriches it in place (SoldDateUtc = the parsed sale date; Price backfilled via ??= only if it was null), adding no new row. Only when wasSold is false (the item page reveals a sale search never caught, e.g. an active listing later confirmed sold) does it add a new ListingStatusChangeEntity with Source ListingHistorySource.StatusUpdate, matching ListingUpserter's own active-to-sold transition. A defensive fallback still adds a new row if wasSold is true but no existing Sold row is found (should not occur in practice, since ListingUpserter always writes one).
criteria.plannedVerification: ItemDetailStoreTests.Should_enrich_the_existing_sold_history_row_instead_of_adding_a_duplicate_when_already_sold (review test (a)) seeds a listing IsSold=true with one pre-existing Sold/InitialScrape history row (Price set, SoldDateUtc null, mirroring what ListingUpserter.AddNew writes for a listing first seen in a sold search), applies a sold item-page detail, and asserts exactly one Sold-status history row still exists, with SoldDateUtc set to the parsed sale date and Price backfilled. ItemDetailStoreTests.Should_add_exactly_one_sold_row_when_an_active_listing_is_revealed_sold_by_the_item_page (review test (b)) seeds a listing stored Active with an Active/InitialScrape history row, applies a sold item-page detail, and asserts exactly one new Sold-status row is added with Source StatusUpdate and the parsed SoldDateUtc. SoldListingFromSearchGetsSoldDateAndHistoryFromDetailFetchTests was extended to seed the same pre-existing Sold/InitialScrape row a real sold-search run would have left (via ListingUpserter) before running ItemDetailFetchService end to end, and now asserts exactly one Sold-status row exists (rather than counting rows by Source), carrying the fixture's parsed SoldPrice/SoldDateUtc. Observable outcome: the status-change history has exactly one row per real state transition, so anything counting sales from history is no longer double-counted, and old-app parity (one row per transition) is restored.

comparisonObservation.firstObservation: A listing already marked Sold before detail fetch (wasSold=true) gets its existing Sold history row enriched in place with SoldDateUtc/Price; no new row is added.
comparisonObservation.whenHeldValueAbsent: A listing not yet marked Sold before detail fetch (wasSold=false, the transition the item page itself reveals) gets exactly one new Sold/StatusUpdate history row added.

criteria.verificationStatus: verified: ItemDetailStoreTests.Should_enrich_the_existing_sold_history_row_instead_of_adding_a_duplicate_when_already_sold and Should_add_exactly_one_sold_row_when_an_active_listing_is_revealed_sold_by_the_item_page both passed against real SQLite; SoldListingFromSearchGetsSoldDateAndHistoryFromDetailFetchTests.Should_end_the_run_with_sold_date_sold_price_and_a_history_row_for_a_listing_a_sold_search_already_marked_sold passed against real SQLite with the extended pre-existing-history-row seed

criteria.criterion: A listing already detailed is not fetched again by later runs.
criteria.plannedImplementation: ItemDetailStore.GetListingsNeedingDetail filters on l.DetailFetchedUtc == null, and ApplyItemDetail / MarkDetailFetchFailed both set DetailFetchedUtc = DateTime.UtcNow on every outcome (success or failure), so a listing is a fetch target exactly once regardless of run boundaries.
criteria.plannedVerification: AlreadyDetailedListingIsNotRefetchedByLaterRunsTests.Should_not_fetch_a_listing_again_once_it_already_has_a_detail_fetch_timestamp seeds a listing with DetailFetchedUtc already set, runs ScrapeRunService again with an IScrapeClient that throws if invoked, and asserts the run completes without the client being called and the listing's fields are unchanged. Observable outcome: repeated nightly runs never re-fetch a listing's item page once it has been detailed.

criteria.criterion: A failed item fetch marks that listing failed and does not fail the run, and stays eligible for retry on later runs up to a small attempt limit rather than permanently losing detail (review fix: the scraper returns a Cloudflare interstitial on roughly 1 in 3 Mercari fetches today (AIOWebScraper #148), and the original design's DetailFetchedUtc stamp on every failure made that permanent for about a third of listings).
criteria.plannedImplementation: Added a non-nullable DetailFetchAttempts int column to ListingEntity (default 0), via an EF-generated migration 20260924003128_AddListingDetailFetchAttempts (internal, auto-generated header, ordered after 20260924000124_AddSchedulerState, backfills existing rows to 0). DetailFetchOptions gained MaxDetailFetchAttempts (default 3, configurable via Scrape:MaxDetailFetchAttempts). ItemDetailStore.MarkDetailFetchFailed now increments DetailFetchAttempts and, only once it reaches maxAttempts, sets DescriptionStatus="failed"; it never sets DetailFetchedUtc, which stays null until a fetch actually succeeds. GetListingsNeedingDetail's WHERE clause changed from DetailFetchedUtc == null alone to DetailFetchedUtc == null && DetailFetchAttempts < maxAttempts, and its ordering changed from OrderBy(Id) to OrderBy(DetailFetchAttempts).ThenBy(Id), so never-attempted listings (0 attempts) always sort ahead of previously-failed ones under a tight per-run cap. ItemDetailFetchService threads _options.MaxDetailFetchAttempts through to both GetListingsNeedingDetail and every MarkDetailFetchFailed call site (blocked page, parse-null, client-throw).
criteria.plannedVerification: ItemDetailStoreTests.Should_increment_attempts_and_stay_eligible_without_marking_failed_on_a_single_failure asserts one failure increments DetailFetchAttempts to 1, leaves DetailFetchedUtc null and DescriptionStatus not yet "failed". Should_mark_the_listing_failed_once_attempts_reach_the_configured_maximum calls MarkDetailFetchFailed three times (max=3) and asserts DescriptionStatus becomes "failed", DetailFetchedUtc stays null, and the listing is no longer returned by GetListingsNeedingDetail. Should_prefer_never_attempted_listings_over_previously_failed_ones_when_the_cap_is_tight seeds one previously-failed listing and one never-attempted listing, requests a cap of 1, and asserts only the never-attempted listing is selected. FailedItemFetchMarksListingFailedWithoutFailingTheRunTests was updated to configure MaxDetailFetchAttempts=1 (so a single blocked fetch immediately exhausts the limit, preserving the test's original run-still-completes intent) and now asserts DetailFetchedUtc stays null on the failed listing alongside DescriptionStatus="failed". ItemDetailFetchServiceTests' three failure-path tests (parse-null, client-throw, no-parser-match) were updated to the new 4-argument GetListingsNeedingDetail/3-argument MarkDetailFetchFailed store signatures. Observable outcome: a listing blocked once is retried on a later run instead of permanently losing description, seller and shipping detail; only a listing that keeps failing past the attempt limit is given up on.
materialConcerns: The listing-level DescriptionStatus stays whatever it last was (typically null/unset) while attempts remain below the limit, so a caller reading DescriptionStatus alone cannot yet distinguish never-attempted from in-retry; DetailFetchAttempts on the same row disambiguates this and was left as the source of truth for retry state rather than introducing a third DescriptionStatus value the ticket did not ask for.
criteria.verificationStatus: verified: ItemDetailStoreTests.Should_increment_attempts_and_stay_eligible_without_marking_failed_on_a_single_failure, Should_mark_the_listing_failed_once_attempts_reach_the_configured_maximum and Should_prefer_never_attempted_listings_over_previously_failed_ones_when_the_cap_is_tight all passed against real SQLite; FailedItemFetchMarksListingFailedWithoutFailingTheRunTests.Should_mark_the_blocked_listing_failed_and_still_apply_detail_to_the_listing_that_succeeds passed against real SQLite with MaxDetailFetchAttempts=1; ItemDetailFetchServiceTests failure-path tests all passed with the updated store signatures; dotnet ef migrations list confirms 20260924003128_AddListingDetailFetchAttempts is ordered after 20260924000124_AddSchedulerState; dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes reports none

criteria.criterion: Concurrency and per-run cap are honoured (test with a stub client counting in-flight calls).
criteria.plannedImplementation: ItemDetailFetchService.FetchDetails requests at most DetailFetchOptions.MaxDetailFetchesPerRun targets from the store, then bounds concurrent fetches with a SemaphoreSlim sized to DetailFetchOptions.MaxConcurrentDetailFetches (floored at 1) around Task.WhenAll. ServiceCollectionExtensions.BuildDetailFetchOptions reads Scrape:MaxConcurrentDetailFetches (default 4) and Scrape:MaxDetailFetchesPerRun (default 50) from configuration.
criteria.plannedVerification: DetailFetchHonoursConcurrencyAndPerRunCapTests.Should_fetch_only_up_to_the_per_run_cap_and_leave_the_rest_for_a_later_run seeds more undetailed listings than the configured per-run cap, runs detail fetch against a real SQLite database, and asserts exactly the cap's-worth of listings received DetailFetchedUtc while the remainder are left for a later run. ItemDetailFetchServiceTests.Should_never_exceed_the_configured_concurrency_limit_while_fetching_details uses ConcurrencyTrackingScrapeClient (an IScrapeClient test double tracking peak concurrent in-flight calls via an Interlocked CAS loop) to assert the observed peak concurrency never exceeds MaxConcurrentDetailFetches, and Should_pass_the_per_run_cap_as_the_fetch_limit asserts GetListingsNeedingDetail is called with the configured cap as its limit argument. Observable outcome: a large backlog of undetailed listings spreads fetch load across nights instead of hammering the marketplace in one run.
criteria.verificationStatus: verified: DetailFetchHonoursConcurrencyAndPerRunCapTests.Should_fetch_only_up_to_the_per_run_cap_and_leave_the_rest_for_a_later_run passed against real SQLite; ItemDetailFetchServiceTests.Should_never_exceed_the_configured_concurrency_limit_while_fetching_details and Should_pass_the_per_run_cap_as_the_fetch_limit both passed
